name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> for battle-AI tile scanning. 'collect_unmarked_tile_positions' accurately describes the body: collect (x,y) of tiles whose overlay byte +7 != 0xFF (i.e. not marked). No address residue; consistent with siblings fd2_mark_char_occupant_tiles_for_team / fd2_scan_chars_*.
purpose: Enumerate every battle tile whose overlay byte +7 is not 0xFF and write its (x,y) byte-pair into the output buffer, returning the tile count; gathers the reachable, unoccupied tile set callers use for AI movement/AoE candidate scans.
logic_summary: count=0; tile_ptr = tile_map_ptr + 7 (overlay byte at +7 within each 4-byte tile entry). Nested loop y in [0,map_height_tiles), x in [0,map_width_tiles): if *tile_ptr != 0xFF, write (uint8)x to out_buf[0] and (uint8)y to out_buf[1], advance out_buf by 2, count++. tile_ptr advances by 4 each inner step (tile entry stride). Return count. Prologue calls __CHK(0x10) (stack probe). Counterpart to fd2_mark_char_occupant_tiles_for_team: callers run fd2_init_movement_range_floodfill (reachable tiles keep +7, unreachable set to 0xFF) then mark occupant tiles 0xFF beforehand, so 'unmarked' == reachable AND unoccupied.

params.name: param_1
params.semantics: Output buffer pointer; receives one (x_byte, y_byte) pair per collected tile (2 bytes each). Src home file already names it 'out_buf'.
params.reason: Live Ghidra still has generic placeholder 'param_1'; rename to 'out_buf' (already used in src home file) to match its role as the output (x,y)-pair buffer. Stage 2 applies the Ghidra rename.

returns.semantics: Number of collected tiles (count of unmarked tiles, i.e. tiles with overlay byte +7 != 0xFF). Equals the number of (x,y) byte-pairs written to out_buf.

comment_original_issue: Original src comment was mechanically correct ('Collect all tiles whose overlay byte +7 is not 0xFF. Write (x,y) byte-pairs to out_buf, return count.') but omitted the semantic role: that 'unmarked' is meaningful only because callers first floodfill reachability and mark occupant tiles 0xFF, so the result is the reachable, unoccupied tile set.
notes: Verified via disassembly (0x14b16): MOV EDX,[0x53a51](tile_map_ptr)+7; outer bound [0x53ac5]=map_height_tiles, inner bound [0x53ac1]=map_width_tiles; MOVZX byte then CMP 0xFF (byte compare, decompiler's '(char*) != -1' is equivalent to src '*tile_ptr != 0xFF'); writes BL(x)/CL(y), ADD EAX,2, INC ESI(count), ADD EDX,4 (stride). 4 callers all consume buffer as (x,y) byte-pairs to score reachable candidate tiles: fd2_ai_walk_to_target_tile, fd2_ai_score_physical_attack, fd2_ai_score_item_use, fd2_ai_score_offensive_spell. Ghidra plate is detailed and consistent (its speculative 'animation scatter positions' use is an unconfirmed 'or' but not contradictory), left unchanged.
